proposed.what: Whether the reflection symmetry of the problem (R is invariant under h[i] -> h[n-1-i]) is exploited in the parametrisation of the shape
alternatives: Impose h[i]=h[n-1-i], optimise half the vector, mirror at the end
Optimise freely, then symmetrise about the peak and polish again
Leave the heights a free asymmetric vector (what all six do)

proposed.what: Whether more than one candidate shape is alive at a time (trajectory count / population)
alternatives: Keep K shapes, select and recombine the best periodically
Run K independent restarts inside the budget, return the best exact R
One chain from one starting point, as every program here does

proposed.what: Whether the breakpoint geometry of the step function is a degree of freedom: all programs fix equal-width cells anchored at the start of the support, so widths, positions and grid phase never vary
alternatives: Let cell boundaries be free continuous variables (non-uniform widths)
Optimise a global sub-cell offset/phase of the whole support
Keep equal-width cells fixed from the interval start (current behaviour)

proposed.what: Whether the location of ||f*f||_inf (which knots attain the max, or a near-max plateau) is tracked across iterations or recomputed from scratch each probe
alternatives: Freeze the argmax index and solve a smooth problem on the rest, then re-check
Track the set of near-max knots and treat them as an active plateau constraint
Recompute the global max after every accepted move (all programs here)

proposed.what: The time budget is enforced the same way: a deadline from time.process_time() checked inside the inner iteration loop, iterating until it is near
alternatives: Deadline checked every outer phase instead of every inner step
Wall-clock timers with a safety divisor
Fixed iteration cap calibrated once from a timing run

alternatives: Return a rescaled/normalised best vector
Store heights as float32 or a list
Round tiny heights to zero before returning
